issuer: Merced Irrigation District Water & Hydroelectric System Refunding Revenue Bonds, Series 2014A
pledge: NET REVENUES = Net Water System Revenues + Net Hydroelectric System Revenues (Revenues of each system minus its O&M). The retail Energy System (electric distribution, ~8,000 customers, $80.0M of 2005/2012/2013 obligations) is SEPARATE and its revenues are NOT pledged and NOT available for these bonds. Hydro-vs-water split: FY2014 actual revenue was almost entirely Water System (water sales $12.0M + transfers $3.9M + 1% property tax $2.9M); hydro contributed little (cost-reimbursement only) because the PG&E power contract had expired. Projections (FY15-19) assume merchant hydro energy sales of $6.3-8.8M vs water sales $17-22M, i.e. ~25-30% of pro-forma revenue is HYDRO and is merchant-priced + hydrology-dependent. OS expressly warns: 'Lower electric rates and reduction in water flow through the Hydroelectric System could result in materially lower Hydroelectric System revenues.' Water side is a strong agricultural irrigation district: pre-1914 Merced River water rights, 605,000 AF storage licenses, ~164,000 irrigated acres, pop ~140,000, 2,200+ customers, $3.15M annual standby-charge revenue.
lien: Senior/first lien on Net Revenues. After this 2014 refunding NO parity obligations remain outstanding. The 2005 Bonds/2005 Installment Payments are pledged Net Hydroelectric Revenues SUBORDINATE to the 2014 Bonds. (Note: only the small $725k taxable 2014B series is junior to certain Energy obligations on hydro net revenues; OUR bond is the tax-exempt 2014A and has the clean senior claim.)
rate_covenant: Net Revenues (Net Water + Net Hydro combined) >= 125% of Debt Service each Fiscal Year, with the proviso that Rate-Stabilization-Fund transfers IN to revenues are capped at 25% of debt service for covenant purposes. Historic Water-System-only coverage on the small 2008 debt was 3.22x (FY2014)/1.78x (FY2013). Projected combined coverage on the larger 2014 debt (~$2.74M/yr) is 3.0-3.3x but that leans on the merchant-hydro revenue materializing.
dsrf: SURETY. Reserve Fund Requirement $2,405,740.25 satisfied by an AGM (Assured Guaranty Municipal Corp.) municipal-bond debt-service-reserve insurance policy, not cash. Separately a Rate Stabilization Fund seeded ~$1,500,000 cash at closing.
abt: Additional parity bonds permitted (Additional Indebtedness caption) subject to a Net-Revenues coverage test; District covenants no parity senior to 2014 Bonds beyond the indenture's ABT. Subordinate hydro pledges (2005 obligations) and an unsecured $25M Wells Fargo line are carved out as junior/unsecured.
insurance: Insured by Assured Guaranty Municipal Corp. (AGM). Underlying rating not separately printed on the EMMA security page (shows S&P insured rating). DSRF also AGM surety.
oid: Yes - modest original issue discount (offered at 97.873, i.e. ~2.13 pts below par). De-minimis-relevant but shallow at issue; current deep secondary discount is a rate-driven mark, not an OID matter.
adverse_notes: (1) HYDRO MERCHANT/HYDROLOGY RISK is the principal credit variable: ~25-30% of pro-forma pledged revenue is merchant hydro post-PG&E-contract; a dry-year + low-power-price combination compresses coverage. (2) FERC relicensing - at issuance the Merced River Hydroelectric Project operated under annual FERC licenses pending a long-term license; continued ops depend on FERC renewals. (3) Mariposa Settlement litigation could reduce hydro revenue (flagged in litigation section). (4) DSRF is a surety (AGM), not cash - reserve quality is only as good as AGM. (5) Standby/property-tax revenue ($2.9M 1% property tax) is a meaningful non-rate revenue component. None of these are masking - all disclosed; water-system base alone historically covered the legacy debt.
issue_price_basis: EMMA Security/Details initial offering field + OS cover/inside-cover.

issuer: California Municipal Finance Authority Wastewater Revenue Bonds, Series 2014 (Humboldt Community Services District Project)
pledge: CONDUIT pass-through. CMFA (the Authority) issues; the Bonds are limited obligations of CMFA payable SOLELY from Installment Payments made by Humboldt Community Services District under an Installment Sale Agreement (Wastewater System), dated 11/1/2014. The Installment Payments are secured by a pledge of the SYSTEM NET REVENUES OF THE WASTEWATER SYSTEM ONLY (Gross Wastewater Revenues - M&O). NOT the District's water system, NOT general fund, NOT taxing power. At the District level the obligation is expressly a 'special obligation payable solely from System Net Revenues' - the District is NOT required to advance any other money. Whose credit: Humboldt CSD's wastewater enterprise (small community-services district serving the unincorporated area around Eureka - Myrtletown, Cutten, Rosewood, Pine Hill, King Salmon, etc.; ~9,525 dwelling units at project buildout).
lien: PARITY (not first). The 2014 Installment Payments are on a PARITY with the 2012 Installment Agreement (original $4,487,000). Additional parity obligations permitted under the ABT. So senior-lien claim is SHARED with the 2012 debt on wastewater net revenues.
rate_covenant: Dual test: System Net Revenues >= 120% of Installment Payments + Debt Service on parity obligations each Fiscal Year; AND >= 100% including all obligations under the Installment Sale Agreement (excluding connection fees and rate-stabilization transfers from the 120% numerator). PRO-FORMA HISTORICAL wastewater coverage was thin and volatile: 1.03x (FY09), 0.87x (FY10, BELOW 1.0x), then 4.42x/3.99x/5.12x (FY11-13) as net revenues rose from ~$95k to ~$1.0M. PROJECTED pro-forma coverage WITH the 2014 bonds settles to ~2.24x (FY15) then 1.54x-1.55x (FY16-18) on net revenues ~$1.1M - above the 120% covenant but a thin cushion.
dsrf: SURETY. Reserve Account Requirement $487,775, satisfied at delivery by an AGM (Assured Guaranty Municipal Corp.) debt-service-reserve insurance policy, not cash. Surety/LC providers must be rated in the three highest categories.
abt: Parity obligations permitted on a 120% MADS coverage test (Certificate of the District): historic test = System Net Revenues for the most recent audited FY or any 12 of the prior 18 months >= 120% of MADS on all outstanding 2014 + parity + proposed obligations; OR projected first-year >= 120%; proceeds must finance the System; opinion of counsel; no default. Refunding carve-out (no DS increase) is exempt from the test.
insurance: Insured by Assured Guaranty Municipal Corp. (AGM); financial-strength AA (S&P, stable)/A2 (Moody's, stable) at issuance (affirmed 7/2/2014). No underlying District rating shown in the OS body. The OS notes AGM ratings were on possible watch for downgrade.
issue_price: 98.295% / 4.10% yield (initial offering field on EMMA for this 4% 06/01/2044 term bond). The 2044 maturity is a TERM bond with mandatory sinking-fund redemption FY2040-2044 ($400k-$465k/yr).
oid: Yes - modest original issue discount (offered 98.295, ~1.7 pts below par). Shallow at issue; current deep secondary discount is rate-driven.
adverse_notes: (1) SMALL, THIN-COVERAGE SYSTEM: pro-forma coverage only ~1.54x post-financing on ~$1.1M net revenues; one prior year (FY10) was below 1.0x. (2) PARITY 2012 debt shares the lien - not a clean first lien. (3) CONSTRUCTION-RISK BOND: proceeds finance Phases 2b/2c of the Martin Slough Interceptor; at issuance the prior contractor (Apex Directional Drilling) had abandoned the job and was in litigation (Apex's $6.3M suit vs the City; District's MAX exposure estimated ~$2.1M if Apex prevails). (4) NO STANDBY CHARGES/ASSESSMENTS on the wastewater system - rate increases are fully exposed to Prop 218 majority-protest, so rate-covenant compliance depends on the District's ability to raise user rates. (5) Pure revenue conduit - NO CMFA recourse, NO general-fund or ad-valorem backstop, NO District obligation to advance other funds; recovery in default is limited to wastewater net revenues + judicial remedies (acceleration without assured funds). (6) AGM-wrapped, so the marketed rating is AGM's; underlying is unrated/weak. None of this is masking - all disclosed in Risk Factors and Table 6/7; but this is a structurally junior-economics small-system credit relative to the Merced or West Hills names.

issuer: West County Facilities Financing Authority 2021 Wastewater Revenue Bonds (Green Bonds)
pledge: INSTALLMENT-SALE / Marks-Roos JPA. West County Facilities Financing Authority (a JPA of West County Wastewater District + CSCDA, formed 8/1/2021) issues; bonds payable from Installment Payments made by WEST COUNTY WASTEWATER DISTRICT under an Installment Purchase Agreement (9/1/2021). The Installment Payments are a special obligation of the District, secured by a pledge of and FIRST LIEN on ALL NET REVENUES of the District's wastewater Enterprise (Gross Revenues - O&M). Gross Revenues are broad: all sewer charges PLUS the District's share of County property-tax/tax-increment (redevelopment) allocation PLUS investment earnings; EXCLUDES connection fees and ad-valorem taxes levied to pay GO bonds. Underlying agency = West County Wastewater District (sanitary district founded 1921; western Contra Costa County - San Pablo, parts of Pinole and Richmond, Tara Hills, North Richmond, El Sobrante, etc.; 16.9 sq mi, ~34,000 residences + ~900 commercial, pop ~104,000). DIVERSIFIED ratepayer base: top-10 customers only 11.2% of charges, largest (EBMUD) 4.4%. ~91% of sewer revenue is FLAT charges (consumption-independent, drought-resilient). Billed on the County property-tax roll under a TEETER PLAN -> District receives 100% of billed amounts, no delinquency exposure.
lien: FIRST LIEN on Net Revenues, SHARED on a PARITY with four 2015 SWRCB State Revolving Fund (SRF) Loans (~$35.1M total outstanding at 1.0-1.9%). The District covenants it will NOT issue any obligation SENIOR to the Installment Payments (no senior debt permitted). Subordinate debt is permitted under a separate 100% MADS test.
rate_covenant: Net Revenues (Gross + Rate-Stabilization-Fund transfers - O&M) >= 120% of Installment Payments + parity DS each Fiscal Year, layered on a sum-sufficient cascade (pay O&M first, then IPs+parity, then other indenture amounts, then additional payments). PRO-FORMA coverage (Table 12) is strong: historical 7.65x/6.90x/4.09x on the small SRF-only DS, settling to ~2.25x/2.49x/2.29x then ~1.64x/1.73x/1.76x (FY24-26) once the 2021 Revenue Bonds (~$4.78M/yr DS) layer on top - comfortably above the 120% covenant. CAVEAT: FY2020-21 AUDITED net revenues dipped to $4.85M (elevated O&M + a depressed year); against post-bond total DS ~$7.49M that single year would have been ~0.65x. The projected 1.6-1.8x recovery DEPENDS on the adopted 5.5%/yr (then 3%) rate increases being realized - rate execution is the key variable.
dsrf: NONE. This deal has NO debt-service reserve fund - the TOC and Security section carry only a Rate Stabilization Fund (held by the District, NOT pledged to the bonds), no Reserve Fund/surety. Unusual vs the older insured deals; consistent with a strong-underlying-rating uninsured structure.
abt: 120% MADS test. New parity obligations require: no default; AND Net Revenues for the most recent 12 months (ending <=60 days before adoption) >= 120% of Maximum Annual Debt Service on the Installment Payments + all parity to be outstanding (Additional Revenues may be added). Refunding parity that lowers aggregate DS is exempt from (a)/(b). Subordinate obligations allowed on a 100% MADS test.
insurance: NONE (uninsured). UNDERLYING ratings are strong on their own: S&P AA- and Moody's Aa3 assigned directly to the bonds. Kestrel Verifiers 'Green Bond' second-party opinion (ICMA Green Bond Principles) - a use-of-proceeds label, NOT a credit enhancement.
issue_price: 120.624% / 1.68% yield (initial offering field on EMMA for this 4% 06/01/2041 maturity). The overall issue ($79,575,000) was sold at a large net original-issue PREMIUM ($16,157,183 premium; UW purchase price $95,602,095.50 = par - $130,088 discount + $16.16M premium). Underwriter Piper Sandler & Co.
oid: No - this is a PREMIUM bond (120.6% at issue). De-minimis-favorable (premium amortizes, no ordinary-income accretion). Current deep secondary discount is a rate-driven mark, not OID.
adverse_notes: (1) NO DEBT-SERVICE RESERVE FUND - in a stress year there is no cash cushion behind the bonds; relies on the Rate Stabilization Fund (unpledged) and rate-covenant enforcement. (2) ~$35M of PARITY SRF loans share the first lien (not a clean sole-lien). (3) PRO-FORMA COVERAGE leans on adopted rate increases; the FY21 audited low year would have been sub-1.0x post-bond, so the credit is 'fine if rates rise as planned, thin if they don't' - though 91%-flat-charge revenue + Teeter 100%-collection + AA-/Aa3 underlying mitigate. (4) CONTINUING-DISCLOSURE HISTORY GAP: 'Neither the District nor the Authority have undertaken responsibilities with regard to Rule 15c2-12 to provide annual reports or notices of listed events in the last five years' - first-time/lapsed filer; monitor that post-2021 Annual Reports are actually being filed on EMMA. (5) HAYWARD FAULT seismic exposure: ~31% chance of M6.7+ in 30 yrs runs under District facilities (Parchester Village force main flagged); IPA does NOT require earthquake/flood insurance. (6) CONSTRUCTION/GREEN-USE bond (force-main + gravity-sewer energy-efficiency project) with capitalized interest through 6/1/2023. All disclosed; on balance the STRONGEST of the four credits (large diversified enterprise, AA-/Aa3 underlying, first lien, Teeter collection).

issuer: West Hills Community College District 2016 General Obligation Refunding Bonds, Series B (School Facilities Improvement District No. 3 - Lemoore Area)
pledge: UNLIMITED AD-VALOREM GENERAL OBLIGATION. CONFIRMED. OS cover and 'SECURITY FOR THE BONDS - General': 'The Boards of Supervisors of the Counties have the power and are obligated to annually levy and collect ad valorem taxes upon all property subject to taxation in the Improvement Districts WITHOUT LIMITATION OF RATE OR AMOUNT (except certain personal property taxable at limited rates) for the payment of principal of and interest on the Bonds.' IMPORTANT STRUCTURAL NUANCE: this Series B is issued by West Hills CCD ON BEHALF OF its School Facilities Improvement District No. 3 (Lemoore Area). The unlimited ad-valorem levy is on the SFID No. 3 territory ONLY (collected primarily by Kings County, with a Fresno County portion) - NOT the District-wide tax base. All District GO bonds (across the District and SFID Nos. 1/2/3) are issued on a PARITY with one another with respect to tax levies. User note confirmed: a community college district, NOT under the K-12 AB-1200 fiscal-oversight regime.
lien: Statutory unlimited-tax GO levy; separate Debt Service Fund per series maintained by the County. Parity tax-levy status with other District/SFID GO bonds. Not a debt of the County or State.
rate_covenant: N/A for a GO - secured by the mandatory unlimited ad-valorem levy, not a revenue rate covenant. The tax rate floats to whatever is needed to pay fixed debt service against the SFID No. 3 assessed valuation each year.
dsrf: N/A (GO - no debt-service reserve fund; security is the unlimited tax levy). Net refunding proceeds were escrowed to U.S. Bank to advance-refund the 2008 SFID No. 3 bonds.
abt: N/A (GO). New District/SFID GO bonds require voter authorization and are issued on a parity tax-levy basis; this Series B is itself a refunding (no new money, lowers debt service).
insurance: INSURED by Assured Guaranty Municipal Corp. (AGM). INSURED RATING S&P 'AA'; UNDERLYING RATING S&P 'A+' (per cover page). Solid underlying GO credit independent of the wrap.
issue_price: 98.759% / 4.08% yield (initial offering field on EMMA for this 4% 08/01/2041 maturity; a term bond with mandatory sinking-fund redemption). The Series B was a $14,455,000 issue (advance-refunding the 2008 SFID No. 3 Series B 2041 term bond, $7,950,000 refunded at 100% on 08/01/2021 per supplement).
oid: Yes - modest original issue discount (98.759, ~1.24 pts below par at issue). Shallow; current deep secondary discount is rate-driven.
adverse_notes: (1) SMALLER, SFID-SPECIFIC tax base: the levy rides on SFID No. 3 (Lemoore Area) AV, not the whole ~$16.2B District - though SFID No. 3 AV has grown strongly to $7.35B (2025-26) from $4.50B local-secured (2016-17). (2) CONCENTRATED CENTRAL-VALLEY ECONOMY: agricultural + food-processing (Leprino Foods 6.10% of SFID No. 3 secured AV) + oil & gas; AV is sensitive to ag commodity cycles, oil-price-driven oil/gas property reassessment, and Prop 8 decline-in-value appeals. (3) TEETER nuance: Fresno County Teeters the District's GO levy (100% receipt) but Kings & Monterey do NOT - and SFID No. 3 is largely in Kings County, so collection depends on actual Kings County receipts (though FY24-25 SFID No. 3 secured delinquency was 0.00%). (4) Pension/OPEB: District-wide unrestricted NET POSITION is negative (-$27.5M FY15, GASB 68/75) - normal for a CA public entity and NOT a concern for an unlimited-tax GO. None of this is masking. AGM-wrapped with a solid A+ underlying; the fiscal gap is largely closed by current continuing disclosure (FY2025 annual report filed 03/14/2026).
fiscal_indicators: SFID No. 3 (Lemoore Area) Total Assessed Valuation: $7,348,132,747 (2025-26; local secured $6,731,869,081 + utility $20,546,872 + unsecured $595,716,794) - vs $4,495,752,459 local-secured at the 2016 OS (FY2016-17), i.e. ~50% AV growth over ~9 years. SFID No. 3 secured tax delinquency FY2024-25: 0.00% (Kings County portion). SFID No. 3 top-20 taxpayers = 21.03% of secured AV; largest Leprino Foods 6.10% (food processing). DISTRICT-WIDE Total AV: $16,222,962,185 (2025-26, across Fresno/Kings/Madera/Monterey/San Benito). District FTES recovered to 5,870 (FY2024-25) after a COVID dip (4,568 FY21-22). Gann/Revenue Limit ~$55,945,207 budgeted FY2025. GENERAL FUND: at the 2016 OS, FY2015 audited UNRESTRICTED General Fund balance ~$4.0M (~11% of unrestricted GF expenditures - exceeds the State Chancellor's 5% recommended minimum); the current audited GF balance is in the separately-filed FY2025 audit (referenced as Exhibit A but filed as a stand-alone document on EMMA, not pulled here). District represents no concern re Fresno County Pooled Investment Fund. Continuing disclosure is CURRENT (timely annual reports, FY2025 report posted 03/14/2026) - the unverified-fiscal gap is largely closed and the AV trajectory is strongly positive.
